assessment.answer: The 0.640 score comes from a net loss of $137.7 million (-16% of assets, 9th peer percentile), operating cash burn of $106.4 million, tiny revenue (4th percentile) and a current ratio of 0.58 against a peer median of 0.8. Leverage of 0.69 is close to the peer median of 0.68, so it does not explain the score. The filings show the distress is real and worse than the numbers suggest. Year-end cash of $22.6 million covers only about 2.5 months at the FY2024 burn (~$8.9M/month), or about 4.9 months at the Q4 2024 burn (~$13.9M, ~$4.6M/month). Even adding the ~$13.4M January 2025 offering and keeping the $10.0M minimum liquidity covenant, usable cash lasts roughly 3 to 6 months. Meanwhile the company says it knows of no financing sources, has been delisted from the NYSE, and openly names bankruptcy protection as a possible outcome.
moved_by: Cash of $22.6M against ~$106.4M annual operating burn (Q4 2024 burn ~$13.9M) leaves roughly 2.5 to 5 months of runway, and a $10.0M monthly minimum liquidity covenant cuts the usable amount further
The 10-K explicitly says the company may need to file for bankruptcy protection and that it is aware of no sources of financing (including for the ~$173M DOE base equity contribution)
NYSE trading was suspended on February 26, 2025 and the shares moved to the OTCQX; the noteholder waivers treating OTC as an Eligible Market run only through April 30, 2025

The 10-K warns that any strategic transaction may assign limited or no value to existing equity, and the dominant secured lender Glencore (~66% fully diluted) sent a letter on March 14, 2025 expressing interest in a transaction. This is a typical setup for a court-supervised sale or restructuring.
Mechanic's liens of about $64.0M plus $36.0M plus $5.1M, MasTec's $48.7M arbitration and foreclosure action, and $89.7M of incurred but unpaid Rochester Hub costs

Substantially all assets are already pledged, which leaves little room for new secured debt. The DOE loan cannot be drawn without equity funding that does not exist, and federal disbursements were paused on January 20, 2025.

reasons.reason: Large net loss relative to assets, the input the model weights most
reasons.numbers: net income -$137.7M (-16.0% of assets) vs -$138.0M the year before
reasons.quote: Li-Cycle expects to incur net losses in the future and may never achieve sustained profitability.
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - history of losses

reasons.reason: Heavy operating cash burn that is not shrinking on an annual basis
reasons.numbers: operating cash flow -$106.4M vs -$99.8M; Q4 2024 alone about -$13.9M (106.4 - 92.5)
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31; 10-Q filed 2024-11-07, MD&A - Results of Operations

reasons.reason: Weak short-term liquidity: current assets fell sharply and no longer cover current liabilities
reasons.numbers: current assets $86.4M (from $149.0M) vs current liabilities $150.0M; current ratio 0.58
reasons.peer_comparison: peer median current ratio 0.8; current liabilities at 82nd percentile of assets

reasons.reason: Tiny revenue base that cannot support the cost structure
reasons.numbers: revenue $28.0M (3.3% of assets), up from $18.3M; operating income -$125.5M

reasons.reason: Very little cash left. It lasts about 2.5 months at the FY2024 burn and about 4.9 months at the Q4 2024 burn, and the $10.0M covenant floor shortens both.
reasons.numbers: cash $22.6M at Dec 31, 2024; ~$13.4M net raised January 2025; minimum liquidity $10.0M tested monthly
reasons.quote: As of December 31, 2024, Li-Cycle held cash and cash equivalents of $22.6 million.
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - substantial doubt about going concern

reasons.reason: Management says it needs near-term financing to fund the next twelve months and names bankruptcy as a possible outcome
reasons.quote: may therefore need to significantly modify or terminate operations or dissolve and liquidate its assets under applicable bankruptcy laws or otherwise file for bankruptcy protection.

reasons.reason: The DOE loan is the main path to finishing the Hub, but it cannot be drawn without a ~$173M base equity contribution that has no known source
reasons.numbers: DOE facility up to $475.0M; base equity reserves ~$173.0M; first advance deadline November 7, 2025
reasons.quote: We are presently aware of no such sources of financing to fund the base equity contribution we are required to provide as a condition to drawing on the DOE Loan Facility.
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - DOE Loan Facility

reasons.reason: Possible lender-led transaction with little or no value for equity
reasons.numbers: Glencore letter March 14, 2025; Glencore ~66% fully diluted ownership
reasons.quote: Given the Company’s current financial position, the terms of any such strategic transaction may assign limited or no value to the Company’s existing equity.
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - additional third-party financing

reasons.reason: Delisting from the NYSE hurts the company's ability to raise equity and depends on short-term noteholder waivers
reasons.numbers: suspended February 26, 2025; OTCQX from February 27, 2025; waivers through April 30, 2025
reasons.quote: Trading in the Common Shares on the NYSE was suspended immediately after market close on February 26, 2025.
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - active, liquid trading market

reasons.reason: Large convertible debt far exceeds cash, and PIK interest at ~19-21% effective rates keeps it growing
reasons.numbers: KSP $133.7M; First A&R Glencore $124.1M; Second A&R Glencore $121.8M; Glencore Senior Secured $81.6M
reasons.quote: including an aggregate principal amount of $133.7 million outstanding under the KSP Convertible Note, $124.1 million outstanding under the First A&R Glencore Note
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - ability to service debt

reasons.reason: A thin covenant cushion means a breach could come quickly, followed by acceleration and foreclosure
reasons.numbers: minimum liquidity $10.0M tested monthly vs $22.6M cash
reasons.quote: The Glencore Senior Secured Convertible Note also contains a minimum liquidity covenant that requires us to maintain a minimum amount of liquidity of $10.0 million, tested monthly.
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - Glencore Senior Secured Convertible Note covenants

reasons.reason: Unpaid contractors have filed liens and started arbitration and foreclosure actions on the paused Rochester Hub
reasons.numbers: liens ~$64.0M, $36.0M, $5.1M; MasTec claim $48.7M; cost to complete ~$483.3M including $89.7M incurred but unpaid

reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - Rochester Hub development

reasons.reason: Almost no unpledged collateral is left for new secured borrowing
reasons.quote: we do not have substantial remaining assets available to secure other indebtedness.
reasons.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - secured indebtedness

evidence_against.point: The main debt maturities are not near: KSP is due September 2026 and the Glencore unsecured note May 2027, and interest is paid in kind, so there is no large cash debt payment in the next 12 months
evidence_against.quote: the unsecured convertible note in the principal amount of $200.0 million due May 31, 2027 issued to an affiliate of Glencore plc on May 31, 2022.

evidence_against.point: Interest on the Glencore notes is paid in kind, which saves cash
evidence_against.quote: The Company has elected to pay interest by PIK since the first interest payment on the Glencore Senior Secured Convertible Note on December 31, 2024.

evidence_against.point: A DOE loan facility of up to $475.0M closed, with no principal due before June 2027
evidence_against.quote: On November 7, 2024, Li-Cycle entered into an agreement for a loan facility of up to $475.0 million
evidence_against.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1. Business - Support from Government Programs

evidence_against.point: Glencore, the strategic lender and offtaker, keeps supporting the company: it provided $75M of new money in 2024, gave waivers, and sent a letter of interest in March 2025. An out-of-court takeover by Glencore could avoid a filing.
evidence_against.quote: On March 14, 2025, we received a letter from Glencore, expressing its interest in a potential transaction involving Li-Cycle.
evidence_against.source: 10-K filed 2025-03-31, Item 1A. Risk Factors - additional third-party financing

evidence_against.point: The company still raises small amounts of equity (~$13.4M net in January 2025)
evidence_against.quote: The Company received net proceeds of approximately $13.4 million from the Offering, after deducting the Offering expenses payable by the Company, including the Underwriter’s discounts and commissions.

evidence_against.point: Burn slowed in the second half of 2024 under the Cash Preservation Plan (Q3 -$20.6M vs -$38.7M a year earlier; Q4 about -$13.9M)
evidence_against.quote: Net cash used in operating activities $ (20.6) $ (38.7) $ 18.1 $ (92.5) $ (89.3) $ (3.2)

evidence_against.point: Equity is still positive, and liabilities/assets of 0.69 are in line with peers
